FR-B1: not built: no task or work item carries a Cynefin domain, nothing proposes one and no card asks a person to confirm it, and dispatch runs every task the same way (one builder cell, the standard gate, the independent verifier); it would take a domain on each task, a classifier's proposal confirmed on an Inbox card, and a dispatch and delivery path per domain (scouts for complicated, flagged probes and small canaries for complex, reflexes first for chaotic, refusal for disorder), reusing the verifier, canary and reflexes that already exist.
FR-B2: not built: with no domain classifier there is nothing to run in shadow, no labelled work items to calibrate it on and no calibration score; it would take recording each person-confirmed domain as a label, scoring the classifier's shadow proposals against those labels, and keeping its output out of every gate input (kernel/gate.py judges only tests, trace, fail-first and the verifier today).
FR-B3: not built: there is no domain router, so no routing hypothesis is registered or measured; it would take a pre-registered hypothesis per domain naming the outcome routing should move (first-round warranted rate, escalations, rounds to pass, which kernel/learn.py already computes per builder model for FR-F8), a comparison against unrouted work, and a decision card that removes the router when the difference is not shown.
FR-B4: partly built: the holdout author writes scenarios in the analyst lane from the spec and its interface only, they are stored in the factory's holdout custody outside the project and the product repository, and through a build no builder envelope, lane, commit or person's workspace holds one (FR-B4-AC-1, FR-B4-AC-2); not built: custody across a product-defect ruling, because kernel/rulings.py apply_rulings writes the failing step's method, path and expected values into a visible test criterion ('the holdout scenario for R-1-AC-2 passes: expected {...}'), so the next builder envelope and the contract committed to the product's main carry part of the scenario; keeping it out needs a regression criterion that names the requirement and the failed holdout without its expectations.
